## Natural history notes

A glossy black cobweb spider characterized by a rounded abdomen, long slender legs, and a red hourglass marking on the underside of the abdomen. In Florida, the Southern Black Widow is found in dry sheltered places such as woodpiles, sheds, garages, crawl spaces, rock piles, debris, outdoor furniture, and undisturbed corners around homes and natural areas. It builds an irregular sticky web and feeds on insects and other small arthropods, but it should be treated with caution because females have medically significant venom and can bite defensively if pressed, trapped, or handled.
